text:
jason (Acme Search): Hey team, our nightly ingest is failing since ~02:00 UTC. Indexer shows `400 Bad Request` from the vector DB: "dimension mismatch". We rolled a regress last week but not sure what changed. Any quick ideas? :frowning:

ana (support): Thanks for flagging — can you paste the exact API error and the embedding dims you're sending? Also which model/version the embeddings endpoint returned from?

jason (Acme Search): Error from vector DB: `400: expected vector dim=1536, got 1024`. Our pipeline sends embeddings to /v1/embeddings. We haven't changed our client. We see the payload contains `model: "open-embed-compat-1024"` in the last successful run. But yesterday the embed response started returning models named like `open-embed-1.0-1024-q4` in the body.

mike (eng-ml): Hmm — two possibilities: (1) model pin drift on the Redwood side (we may have a new default variant with 1024 dim), (2) an autoscaling / routing fallback to a cheaper quantized variant that changes dim. Jason, can you share the request you sent (headers + body) and the `model` param you used?

jason (Acme Search): We call: 
```json
{"model":"open-embed-compat","input":"doc text...", "customer_id":"acme-prod"}
```
Headers include `Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-...` and `X-Requested-Batch-ID`. We did not pin a specific numeric variant.

ana (support): That matches a common case: unpinned model requests can route to a compatible variant. But dims should be stable — the model catalog advertises 1536 for `open-embed-compat`. Sophie, any routing logs showing fallback to smaller variants?

sophie (eng-sre): Pulling logs from the serving router. Quick snapshot: around 02:03 UTC we had capacity pressure on the 1536-pool; the router applied a fallback policy to route low-priority traffic to `open-embed-compat-1024` to reduce latency. The embedding API does return the `model` field in the response body, and the dims in the vector payload are 1024. I see many requests in the same batch were truncated to 1024 vectors.

mike (eng-ml): Confirming: we recently onboarded a quantized variant with 1024 dims for memory savings for a subset of customers. Bug here is the router allowed routing to that variant even when the customer downstream expects 1536. We should never silently change vector dimensions for a given customer.

tara (customer-success): Jason — did your team ever pin the `model` param to a specific variant? If not, we should treat this as an out-of-the-box breaking change and prioritize a fix.

jason (Acme Search): We didn't pin. We rely on backwards-compatibility. This is bad — search ingestion backfill can't continue. We're already seeing 12% failed docs.

ana (support): Immediate actions:
1) We'll add a temporary server-side rule to avoid routing `acme-prod` traffic to any 1024-dim variant. (Sophie/infra)
2) Create a short-term backfill plan: drop-in translator to upconvert 1024->1536? (Mike to advise).
3) Longer-term: block variant dim changes for pinned customers and add schema validation to the embeddings responses.

sophie (eng-sre): I've applied a routing override for `customer_id=acme-prod` to force `open-embed-compat` stable pool. Verified no more 1024 responses for new requests. Note: overriding will reduce throughput for that tenant for the next 6 hours while capacity autoscaling catches up.

deploy-bot: Deployment `router-override` succeeded: rollout id `rv-2026-03-15-01` to 4/4 regions.

mike (eng-ml): For the backfill: There is no reliable way to "upconvert" 1024->1536 that preserves vector semantics; nearest option is re-embedding original texts with a 1536 model, or map 1024 vectors into 1536 by padding and fitting — but that will degrade retrieval. Recommend: 1) stop indexing 1024 vectors, 2) queue originals for re-embedding using the pinned 1536 model, 3) mark failed docs and retry. We can provide a temporary shim that rejects 1024 and returns a specific error code to be machine-detected by your pipeline.

jason (Acme Search): Re-embedding the original texts is doable but time-consuming — we have 10M docs. Any option to do incremental backfill?

mike (eng-ml): Yes, incremental backfill by priority is best. Steps:
- identify the high-traffic shards (top 20%) and re-embed those first;
- for the rest, keep the old docs live, but tag them as "legacy-dim" so rankers can weight accordingly;
- run background re-embeds at a throttled rate to avoid blowing your token/billing quotas.

ana (support): On the billing side — we also saw some customers hit unusual token surges because the pipeline retried failed batches. Jason, any retry logic?

jason (Acme Search): Our pipeline retries 3x with exponential backoff. We saw a spike in calls at 02:05 when most failed; that probably pushed us over our burst quota and triggered rate limiting.

sophie (eng-sre): I can see a brief rate-limit 429 wave from the API gateway at 02:06. That's independent but compounding. Two things to do:
- I'll temporarily raise the per-tenant burst quota for `acme-prod` for 2 hours to allow backfill headroom.
- Add a telemetry flag so support can see how many 1024 vectors were generated by customer.

tara (customer-success): I'll notify Jason's ops about the temporary quota bump and recommended backfill cadence. Jason, we'll also assign a Solutions engineer to help run the prioritized re-embed job.

jason (Acme Search): Appreciate it. Can you also confirm whether our auth token or billing status played a part? We got some 401s earlier in the logs too.

ana (support): Checked auth logs: a few short 401 spikes at 01:58 due to a rotated secret on your side; subsequent requests used a refreshed key. No sign the 401s are explaining the dim mismatch — those were 200 responses with 1024 vectors. Billing: your account briefly hit a soft quota on embedding units at 02:07 but didn't get disabled. So root cause = routing to wrong variant + cascading retries causing rate limits.

mike (eng-ml): Next steps (owner tags):
- Sophie: keep routing override until autoscaler fully resizes 1536 pool (in progress) — target ETA 4h.
- Support (ana): update internal incident ticket and flag as P2.
- MGMT/Team: add server-side validation: reject responses where returned vector dim != expected for model name (blocker for silent drift).
- Tara + Solutions: schedule a re-embed plan with Jason and provide a runbook for throttled backfill.

sophie (eng-sre): ETA for autoscaler to add capacity: ~3.5 hours if no additional pressure. I've left the override on and increased burst quota for 2 hours. Will monitor.
deploy-bot: Incident ticket `INC-2026-03-15-1432` created and assigned to `eng-ml` and `eng-sre`.

jason (Acme Search): Thanks team — please keep me posted. We'll start prioritizing the critical shards for re-embed. Can someone post a minimal repro so we can test locally?

mike (eng-ml): Minimal repro steps:
1) call /v1/embeddings without pinning a specific variant: `{"model":"open-embed-compat","input":[...]}"`
2) under serving pressure the router may return `model: "open-embed-compat-1024"` in the response; assert `len(embedding) == 1536` else fail.
3) if you get 1024, don't send to vecDB — requeue for re-embed.

Sample curl:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-compat","input":["test doc"]}'
```
Look at the `model` field and `embedding` length in the JSON response.

ana (support): I'm going to update the support KB with the repro and a recommended client-side guard: check embedding length before sending to vector DB and fail fast with clear logs.

tara (customer-success): I'll coordinate the Solutions engineer to set up a re-embed job and share a timeline with Jason by EOD.

jason (Acme Search): OK closing loop: thanks, please ping in this thread when the autoscaler is healthy. We'll pause indexing until we get the all-clear. :thumbsup:

ana (support): Noted. marking thread as tracking.

sophie (eng-sre): Monitoring now — will post an update at T+60m and T+240m or on notable events.

mike (eng-ml): I'll draft the server-side validation patch and a release note to prevent silent dim changes.

--- end of thread ---
